rationale: Interpreted the applied-state receipt for the split-brain consequence and opened the repair-path question. Receipt fa1f90c2eefd45e6af45d7593ac53205 parsed four events and evaluated all three comparisons: after the partition is healed and one more entry is committed on the surviving leader, the FSM applied state still differs across nodes (violated at witness index 3), with A and C having applied minority-write and B, D and E majority-write while every node's log is at index 13 (operand comparisons hold at index 3). That converts the earlier log-byte divergence into permanently divergent applied state, so the child question's account and the parent account were updated, the same-term divergence fact gained the new receipt as an execution, and a follow-up question now tracks which permitted repair path could reconcile it.

knowledge.statement: Two entries that end up at the same log index with the same term but different payloads on different servers are never reconciled by AppendEntries: the receiver truncates its suffix only when an incoming entry at an existing index has a different term, and an entry whose index and term match the stored one is skipped as a duplicate before any configuration or log processing, so the divergence persists while the cluster continues to commit later entries.
knowledge.conditions: AppendEntries conflict handling (raft.go 1526-1553) on a follower whose stored entry at that index has the same term; observed after the split-leader window of the RestoreCommittedLogs restart defect was healed with a further committed entry and no snapshot install.

interpretations.rationale: The declared predicate is that after the partition is healed every node's FSM has applied the same commands at the index both leaders used; the single witness event contradicts it. Admission index 0 establishes the restart fixture (snapshot index 6 with {A,B,C}, committed configuration entry at index 8 with {A,B,C,D,E}, stored commit index 8). At event index 3, taken after the mesh was reconnected, one further entry was committed and 300 ms passed, the applied write lists are A:minority-write, C:minority-write against B:majority-write, D:majority-write, E:majority-write, so fsm_applied_consistent is false while every node reports log last index 13 and the surviving leader reports the current configuration; the two operand comparisons hold, confirming which side applied which write (a_fsm_applied_writes minority-write, b_fsm_applied_writes majority-write). Mechanism: the entries at index 11 were committed on both sides during the split, and AppendEntries cannot reconcile them because the terms are equal, so each side keeps and applies its own entry; the earlier receipts established the split itself and the same-term log divergence, and this one shows the consequence in applied state. Limits: one healed window after a single further entry, in-memory stores, a graceful restart rather than a crash, and no repair path (installSnapshot, log compaction or user restore) is exercised, so the duration of the divergence is bounded by the observation rather than by evidence; the FSM applied list is read through the MockFSM used by the harness rather than from an application store.
limitations: The applied state is sampled once, one entry after healing; no repair path or long window is covered.
The applied commands are read from the harness FSM (MockFSM), not from an application-level store.
In-memory stores, scaled timeouts and a graceful shutdown instead of a crash.
No no-feature restart control inside the cluster.
counterevidence: The operand comparisons show the majority side applied the write its own leader committed, so the divergence is not an artifact of one node's sampling.
Every node's log is at the same last index after healing, so the applied difference is not explained by one side lagging behind in replication.

interpretations.rationale: Answer: yes, and the damage reaches applied state. A node left with a stale configuration by the RestoreCommittedLogs replay wins an election with fewer votes than the configuration in its own committed log while the other voters elect their own leader; both sides commit at the same index and term, and after healing the FSMs stay different: receipt fa1f90c2eefd45e6af45d7593ac53205 shows A and C having applied minority-write while B, D and E applied majority-write with all five logs at index 13 (violated at index 3, operands holding at the same index), following the split and same-term log divergence recorded in receipts b68f3d3a08b34cd6a27b76faeb0d2a3e and 455e647ad0794a16903414b5a8846276. Mechanism chain: the parent question's configuration scan defect gives the stale quorum, votes come from each voter's own view, and the AppendEntries term comparison cannot reconcile same-term entries, so both sides' FSMs keep their own command at that index. Scope and remaining uncertainty: the applied divergence is reproduced deterministically in local repeats and once formally, but no repair path is exercised, so whether installSnapshot, log compaction or a user restore eventually heals it and whether the library engages such a path on its own is now tracked as a separate question; the no-feature restart control inside the cluster is still unexecuted; and the observation window after healing is short.
limitations: No repair path (installSnapshot, compaction, user restore) is exercised; the divergence's duration is therefore bounded by the observation, not by evidence.
One cluster per run with a single partition window and a short healed sample.
In-memory stores, scaled timeouts and a graceful shutdown rather than a crash.
The no-feature restart control inside the cluster remains unexecuted.
counterevidence: The in-partition control C, with the current configuration, never leads, so the partition alone does not explain the election.
After healing, the cluster elected a node holding the current configuration, so the persistence claim concerns the restarted node's own view and applied state rather than its leadership.
All nodes report the same log last index after healing, so the applied divergence is not explained by replication lag.

interpretations.joint_history: Four receipts of three fixed experiments over one defect chain. The first constructs the restart state in harness-supplied stores and reads the configuration, quorum and FSM queue; the second produces that state through normal operations and observes the split; the third is a revision of the second that adds the healing phase; the fourth is a revision of the third that adds applied-state sampling, and its comparison set is deliberately limited to the three new predicates, so its receipt is not additive evidence for the predicates already recorded with the third. All four share the same structural conditions - snapshot configuration {A,B,C}, a committed configuration entry with {A,B,C,D,E} above the snapshot, a persisted commit index covering it, and a restarted node reporting {A,B,C} (first receipt index 2, second index 0, third index 0, fourth index 0). No value is combined across receipts; each comparison outcome is read from its own receipt.
interpretations.rationale: Current account: with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and a CommitTrackingLogStore whose persisted commit index covers a committed configuration entry newer than the node's last snapshot, NewRaft never rebuilds the node's configuration from that entry, so the restarted node keeps the snapshot's membership for candidate admission and election quorum; that stale view lets it lead with two votes where the current configuration requires three, produces two concurrent leaders whose commits collide at the same index and term, and leaves the applied state on the two sides permanently different until some repair path resets a log or FSM. Basis: restoreFromCommittedLogs reads the persisted commit index and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil) (api.go 724-753); processLogs advances lastApplied to that index (raft.go 1361-1362); the configuration scan then starts at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 (api.go 610-620) above the committed configuration entry, which is never passed to processConfigurationLogEntry; quorum and voter admission come from configurations.latest (raft.go 313-320, 1085-1096, 1660-1680); duplicates are skipped so no later AppendEntries reprocesses the entry or the same-term conflicting command (raft.go 1526-1553); and the persisted commit index exists only because the node ran with the feature enabled (raft.go 1393-1403). Witnesses: receipt f4adc58c4125434eb91cacf438a6da50 for the configuration and quorum state (feature on {A,B,C} with quorum 2, feature off {A,B,C,D,E} with quorum 3), b68f3d3a08b34cd6a27b76faeb0d2a3e for the split and conflicting commits at index 11 term 3, 455e647ad0794a16903414b5a8846276 for the healed log state, and fa1f90c2eefd45e6af45d7593ac53205 for the healed applied state. Remaining limits: no repair path is exercised, so the divergence's eventual fate is now its own question; persistence is observed across one healed window rather than a long run; the restart is graceful with in-memory stores and scaled timeouts; no no-feature restart control was run inside the cluster; and the earlier receipt 99718ab469974eb1ad40516efe7c999e stays a retained channel failure with no evaluated comparison.
limitations: No repair path (installSnapshot, compaction, user restore) is exercised, so the divergence's eventual fate is an open question rather than a bound.
Persistence is observed across one healed window; no long run or further configuration change is covered.
Both cluster experiments use in-memory stores, scaled timeouts and a graceful shutdown instead of a crash.
No no-feature restart control was executed inside the cluster.
counterevidence: The node stores the newer committed configuration entry and replays it to the FSM, so recovery of the configuration through a later configuration entry or an installed snapshot is not excluded; only the observed paths fail to refresh it.
A deployment that never ran with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled stores commit index 0, in which case the scan covers the entry and no divergence occurs.

The in-partition control C never leads in any receipt, and after healing the cluster elected a node holding the current configuration, so the defect explains a minority leader and a persistent stale view plus divergent applied state rather than permanent stale leadership.

investigations.question: Which permitted mechanism reconciles the divergent entries and applied state left by the stale-configuration split: does the library engage installSnapshot, log compaction or a user restore on its own once the cluster is whole, or does the divergence persist while the node participates normally?
investigations.hypothesis: Nothing in the ordinary AppendEntries path reconciles same-term conflicts, and the stale node keeps serving and replicating, so it never falls far enough behind for the leader to send a snapshot; only an explicit snapshot install (forced by compaction plus a lagging follower), a user Restore or a truncation caused by a different term would replace the divergent entry and FSM state.
investigations.discriminator: After the healed split state, force the surviving leader to snapshot and compact past the follower's nextIndex and append one more entry, then sample the divergent index and the applied commands on both sides. Predicted: without intervention the divergence persists, while a snapshot install replaces the restarted node's entry and FSM state with the leader's.
